text.en: The village jatara is tonight. {cast:mentor} presses ₹100 into your hand. Your school notebook is also finished. A new one costs ₹40.

label.en: Buy the notebook first, then enjoy ₹60 of jatara

outcome.en: Notebook: ₹40. Giant wheel: ₹30. Hot jalebi: ₹20. You still have ₹10 and zero guilt.

why.en: A need can't wait; a want can. Cover needs first, and the wants become guilt-free.

label.en: Spend all ₹100 at the jatara

hint.en: Wants first, needs on credit. Small now.

outcome.en: Best night ever. On Monday you have no notebook, so {cast:shopkeeper} writes ₹40 in her [[khata]].

why.en: Spending the need money on wants doesn't remove the need. It just turns it into a debt.

label.en: Save all ₹100 in the tin box

outcome.en: ₹100 saved. But still no notebook, and no jatara. {cast:sibling} brings you half her jalebi.

why.en: Saving everything isn't a plan either. Needs come first, and a small want is allowed.

text.en: {cast:mother} comes back from her [[shg]] meeting. "Our rule: first the savings, then the shopping." Your ₹200 pocket money for the month is in your hand.

label.en: Put ₹40 in the dream jar today, before anything else

outcome.en: ₹40 a month for a year is ₹480. That's a proper cricket bat, with ₹80 left over.

why.en: Save the day money arrives, not at month-end. What you never see, you never spend.

label.en: Spend first, save whatever is left at month-end

hint.en: There is never anything left at month-end.

outcome.en: At month-end, ₹6 is left. At that speed, the ₹400 bat takes over five years.

why.en: Leftovers are tiny because spending fills all the space. Saving first protects your goal.

label.en: Ask Amma to keep ₹20 a month for you

outcome.en: Amma saves ₹20 a month for you: ₹240 by next Sankranti. Her habit, not yours yet.

why.en: Help is good. But saving is a muscle. It grows only when you use it yourself.

text.en: "₹12, kanna," says {cast:shopkeeper}. "It was ₹10 last year." You have ₹300 saved in a tin for a bat that costs ₹300 today.

label.en: Ask Ammamma why prices keep rising

outcome.en: Rice was ₹2 a kilo when Ammamma married. Now it's ₹40. You decide your ₹300 needs a home where it grows.

why.en: [[inflation]] makes prices rise each year. Idle cash buys less and less.

label.en: Buy the bat today, before it costs more

outcome.en: You beat inflation by buying today. Next year the same bat costs ₹318.

why.en: Buying something you really want before prices rise is fine. Just know you're spending, not saving.

label.en: Keep the ₹300 in the tin for three more years

hint.en: The tin box keeps the notes. It doesn't keep their value.

outcome.en: In three years the bat costs ₹357. Your ₹300 is still exactly ₹300.

why.en: At 6% a year, prices go up about a fifth in three years. Cash that doesn't grow falls behind.

text.en: A rat chewed a ₹50 note in your tin box. Next day, {cast:banker} visits school. "Open a [[minor_account]] with a parent. It is zero balance."

truth.en: No minimum amount needed. The account stays open even with ₹0 in it.

label.en: Open the account with Amma and deposit your savings

outcome.en: ₹250 deposited. At 3%, it earns about ₹7 a year. More importantly: no rat can eat it.

why.en: A bank keeps money safe from rats, thieves and impulse buys. And it pays you a little interest.

label.en: Buy a stronger steel box instead

hint.en: {cast:friend} saw where you hid the new box.

outcome.en: The box cost ₹40. It earns ₹0 interest, and everyone at home knows where it is.

why.en: A box at home can't grow money and is easy to raid. A bank is both safe and paid.

label.en: Give the money to Nanna to keep

outcome.en: Nanna keeps it safe for two months. Then the cotton seeds need ₹250, and your savings become seeds.

why.en: Family money gets used for family needs. A separate account keeps your goal yours.

text.en: Nanna needs ₹2,000 for cotton seeds. {cast:lender} smiles: "Only ₹2 per ₹100 a month. Unpaid interest just joins the loan." Nanna looks at you, the maths topper.

truth.en: That is 24% a year. With interest on interest, it is nearly 27%.

phrase.en: Unpaid interest just joins the loan.

truth.en: This is [[chakravaddi]]: next month, you pay interest on the interest too.

label.en: Work out the true cost before Nanna agrees

outcome.en: With [[chakravaddi]], ₹2,000 becomes ₹2,536 in a year. Amma's [[shg]] charges simple 1%: ₹2,240. Nanna borrows from the SHG.

why.en: Compound interest is interest on interest. On debts it grows fast, so always compare the yearly cost.

label.en: Tell Nanna it's only ₹40 a month, that's fine

outcome.en: ₹40 is only the first month. A year later, if unpaid, {cast:lender} wants ₹2,536.

why.en: When interest is added to the loan, the loan grows itself. Small monthly numbers hide big yearly ones.

text.en: A man in small sunglasses shows you a link. "100% free gems! Just tell me the OTP on your Amma's phone." It's {cast:tempter}.

truth.en: Nothing free needs an [[otp]]. The OTP opens Amma's bank account, not a game.

label.en: Read out the OTP from Amma's phone

hint.en: Amma checks her phone twice now, every night.

outcome.en: In one minute, ₹1,800 leaves Amma's account. It was her savings-group instalment. No gems arrive.

why.en: An [[otp]] is a key to your money. Anyone who has it can open the account.

label.en: Close the link and tell Ammamma

outcome.en: Ammamma peers at the link. Fake. You just saved Amma's ₹1,800. "Big glasses, small truth," she says.

why.en: Real banks and games never ask for an OTP. "Free" plus "OTP" always means a trap.

label.en: Forward it to Chintu first

hint.en: Forwarding a trap still sets a trap.

outcome.en: Chintu tries it on his father's phone. ₹2,500 vanishes. He doesn't speak to you for a week.

why.en: Sharing a scam link spreads the harm. Delete it, and warn friends instead.

text.en: {cast:shopkeeper} opens her [[khata]]. "₹40 notebook, plus two biscuit packets, plus one pencil. ₹65, kanna." A year of small credit adds up.

label.en: Pay it from your savings

outcome.en: You pay ₹65. The page is crossed out. It feels better than the jalebi did.

why.en: Credit for small wants grows quietly. Clearing it early keeps it small.

label.en: Ask Amma to pay it

outcome.en: Amma pays ₹65 from the vegetable money. Dinner is a little smaller this week.

why.en: Your debt doesn't disappear when someone else pays. It moves to them.

text.en: {cast:lender} sits on your verandah, very politely. "₹2,000 is now ₹2,536. Bujji is a fine buffalo, Yadagiri." Ammamma's hands are shaking.

label.en: Help Amma take a cheaper SHG loan to pay him off

outcome.en: The SHG lends ₹2,536 at 12% a year. Bujji stays. The costly debt is now a cheap one.

why.en: Swapping a costly loan for a cheaper one stops the [[chakravaddi]] snowball.

label.en: Ask him to wait one more season

hint.en: One more season means one more season of interest.

outcome.en: He agrees. Next season the ₹2,536 is ₹3,217. Bujji is sold in the end.

why.en: Waiting on compound debt makes it grow faster each month. Act early.

text.en: {cast:sibling} runs in with Amma's phone. "Free recharge for kids! It wants the OTP." You remember last year.

label.en: Stop her and explain why

outcome.en: Chinni writes it in her notebook: "OTP = key. Never give. 1930 if stolen." ₹0 lost this time.

why.en: Your mistake became her lesson. That's how families get smarter.

label.en: Let her try, maybe this one is real

outcome.en: ₹600 vanishes. Amma calls 1930 within the hour, and ₹400 is frozen and returned weeks later.

why.en: If cheated online, call 1930 fast. Quick reports often save part of the money.

text.en: {cast:teacher} announces it in assembly: you topped the district maths test. A ₹1,000 merit scholarship!

label.en: Save ₹800, spend ₹200 on a celebration

outcome.en: ₹800 saved, and sweets for the whole class with ₹200.

label.en: Treat everyone to a film in town

hint.en: Windfalls feel like free money. They're still money.

outcome.en: ₹1,000 gone in one glorious afternoon. Chintu still talks about it.

text.en: Bujji the buffalo lies down and won't eat. The vet's medicine costs ₹1,500. Nanna has ₹1,100.

label.en: Give Nanna ₹400 from your savings

outcome.en: Bujji recovers in a week and gives milk again: ₹60 a day for the family.

why.en: Savings are for exactly this. A small cushion stopped a big loss.

label.en: Keep your savings for the dream

outcome.en: Nanna borrows ₹400 from the kirana khata. Bujji recovers. The khata grows.

text.en: An SMS on Nanna's phone: "Congratulations! You won ₹25 lakh in the lucky draw. Pay a ₹999 processing fee to claim."

phrase.en: You won ₹25 lakh in the lucky draw.

truth.en: You never entered any draw. You can't win a lottery you didn't join.

phrase.en: Pay a ₹999 processing fee to claim.

truth.en: Real prizes never ask you to pay first. The fee is the scam.

label.en: Tell Nanna it's fake and delete it

outcome.en: Nanna laughs for the first time this week. "₹25 lakh? We can't even win at carrom."

label.en: Pay the ₹999, just in case it's real

outcome.en: ₹999 gone. Then they ask for ₹4,999 "tax". There is no prize.

text.en: {cast:sibling}'s school uniform tore on the bus. A new one costs ₹350. The same week, the toy car you wanted is on sale for ₹200.

label.en: Put ₹150 towards Chinni's uniform

outcome.en: Chinni wears the new uniform for a full week without sitting down. She writes "best big one" in her notebook.

label.en: Buy the toy car

outcome.en: The car is fast. Chinni's uniform has a safety pin for two months.

text.en: {cast:friend}'s cousin has a deal. "Give me your game password. I'll level you up for free, mama." Amma's card is saved in that game.

phrase.en: I'll level you up for free

truth.en: With your password, anyone can buy things on the saved card. Nobody levels you up for free.

label.en: Share the password, just this once

hint.en: A password shared once is shared forever.

outcome.en: By night, ₹1,200 of top-ups are charged to Amma's card. Your account is gone too.

why.en: A password is a key, like an OTP. Never share it, even with friends.

label.en: Say no, and ask Amma to remove her saved card

outcome.en: Amma removes the card. Next week the cousin's own account is hacked. You lost ₹0.

why.en: Keep passwords secret and don't leave cards saved in games.
